newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk president ask Yilmaz to continue govt search.
newsitem.headline: Turk president ask Yilmaz to continue govt search.

text.p: Turkish conservative Mesut Yilmaz said after a round of talks with the party leaders on Wednesday that the president had asked him to continue his search to form a new government.
"The president asked me to continue in my duty," Yilmaz told reporters after meeting President Suleyman Demirel.

Earlier on Wednesday caretaker Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan hit back at Yilmaz's bid to forge a secularist coalition, presenting a petition signed by a majority of MPs rejecting a plan to keep his Islamists from power.
Deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller urged Yilmaz to return the mandate to form a government to Demirel.
Yilmaz, appointed by the president last week to form a government, is just short of the majority needed to win a confidence vote in the 550-seat parliament.
He has won the backing of secularist MPs from the left and right but will rely on support from dissidents in the rival conservative True Path Party, whose leader Ciller is allied with Erbakan.
